text:
Thomas Chabot is Ottawa's captain and its minute-eater, playing 23.3 a night with 13 points in 23 games. His scoring rate, 1.45 points per 60, is exactly where it was last season and well above the league average for defensemen.

The best part of his season has been the five-on-five share. Ottawa has 58.8% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on the ice, and his relative number is nearly six points better than his teammates. Some luck is helping: the Senators have scored 5.65 more goals than expected with him out there.

His own shooting is the quiet piece. Two goals on 2.71 expected and a 4.8% shooting rate, near the bottom of his range. Evolving-Hockey had him 29th among 215 defensemen last season at 2.0 wins above replacement, almost all of it from even-strength offense, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking found him stopping 16% of the entries aimed at him, above the 11% typical rate. After a 6-5 overtime loss to Philadelphia on November 19, TSN ran his words as its headline: "We have to turn the page and focus on Saturday." Ottawa has won three of four since. Watch whether his own goals start to come.
